The cadet garden used to sit below the east gutter. Each shift was meant to water one bed and leave the next to the person coming after.
I archived the rotation as a table of duties. When the barracks emptied, the table remained and the garden dried out. I kept the record; I never learned how the water reached the roots.
If we can make the bed work again, the next cadets can learn it with their hands. I want them to see what one careful shift leaves for another.
The old slate lists a morning turn, a late turn, and one blank interval after rain. It records where the water was sent, not who stood beside the trough.
A smear of mint green crosses the last entry. Someone added a leaf beside the missing interval, then rubbed the drawing away with a wet thumb.
The empty space can remain empty. The note still tells us that the bed used to be tended after a storm.
I thought the blank interval meant a keeper had failed to report. Now I think the slate only stopped when the work changed hands.
The gutter is still here. If the drain is sound, a new rotation can begin without pretending we know who planted the last bed.
The drain frame is bent at the lower hinge. Rain ran past the garden wall instead of entering the open channel.
The mud holds two parallel grooves. One may be from a tool dragged across the stone; neither groove says who left it there.
I can measure the slope after we clear the mint bed. The frame will need a removable clip so the next person can inspect it.
The old mint still grows in one crack near the eastern step. I saved seed from the patch before the passage was closed.
Plant a small bed and let it finish a full cycle. If the runoff misses it, we will know before anyone uses the slate as a promise.
This Blackreed Trout came from the same lakeshore pool where the gutter drains. Its scales can mark a removable clip, but one fish cannot tell us how clean the water is.
I will keep the catch and the place beside each other in the field note. The mint needs a separate inspection before we call the bed healthy.
The lower stone has a pale line where water reached it after the last rain. The upper scratch may come from the roof hinge, not the channel.
I marked both heights without joining them into a single level. We will compare the next flow after the clip is fitted.
The Blackreed Trout was caught downstream. That confirms its location at the time of the catch, not the source of the water above us.
A rotation works only if the person on the next turn can change it when the weather changes. The old slate has a blank interval because there was no night shift after rain.
Keep one line for the work and another for a handoff. No one should inherit a duty from a name scratched into stone.
The Runoff Clip is ready. The mint fiber pads its jaw, while the trout scale marks the edge that must remain visible above the gutter.
It can be removed without breaking the drain. A keeper should be able to check what passed through, not seal the channel and call it repaired.
The clip fits the bent frame and leaves a narrow gap for leaves and sediment to pass. The marker will remain visible at low water.
This fitting is a maintenance aid, not a water filter. I will compare its mark with the garden bed after the next measured run.
The first runoff reached the upper bed in the short test. A second pour carried grit into the catch pocket; the clip held but needs cleaning after heavy rain.
Elara recorded the time it took to clear the pocket. We have one day of observation, not a seasonal water plan.
The mint is still upright. That is a result from this plot, not proof that every bed on the slope will grow the same way.
A shared bed could let any cadet plant a cutting when they have a free hour. Someone would still need to clear the catch pocket after rain.
I can put the care steps on the slate and leave the next row open for a different plant. The people who use it can decide what belongs there.
We could mark three short turns on the slate and let each training group choose a week. The plot would have a keeper for a while, then return to the next group.
The schedule needs a blank line for weather and a way to step out. A rotation is useful only while it can be changed.
The common-bed sheet lists the water route and the removable clip, then leaves the crop row open. It gives no one a permanent claim over the soil.
I added the day of our runoff test and left a space for the next keeper to repeat it.
The rotation sheet shows three short turns and a pause after heavy rain. Its marks follow the gutter, not the names of the cadets who once carried water.
Anyone taking a turn can amend the day or step out. The unfilled row is part of the schedule, not a missing person.
I used to think an archive began after the work was finished. The garden taught me that a handoff can be part of the record while the water is still moving.
Next week I will ask the cadets to build a second catch pocket, then I will let them decide what to plant beside the mint.
The slate will stay by the door. Anyone can leave a correction before the next turn begins.

The Archive report shows the signal can be measured. It does not tell us who gets to choose what the measurement means.
I want you to trace one resource model from its assumptions to the people living beneath it. Bring back the gaps as carefully as the totals.
The three curves begin with different rainfall and harvest assumptions, but they all use the same demand column.
The blank heading is not zero demand. It is a question the people who made the chart never asked.
The receiver logged pressure changes and the time they arrived. It did not identify a sender or measure what anyone intended.
One clock drifted after the storm. I kept both readings so a later reviewer can see the uncertainty instead of inheriting my correction.
The old estimate counted every seed as food before the plant had taken root. This sample lets us record the time between planting and usable sap.
One plot cannot predict a valley. It can show whether the model keeps seed, growing time and harvest in separate columns.
The ledger says one Farwake Carp came from the Celestial Pool today. That is a catch record, not a count of every fish in the lake.
I will keep the date and spot attached to the sample. We do not know how many fish were missed or how often this result repeats.
The corrected line looks cleaner, but the correction assumes the clock slowed at a steady rate.
I cannot show that from two checks. Keep the raw marks beside the estimate and let the next survey decide whether the drift was steady.
I called the column a witness because it came from a ledger. I had forgotten that the ledger was written for a different purpose.
A record can be accurate about what it counts and still be the wrong evidence for the question we ask of it.
Our ledger marks seed saved for another season in a different color from fruit offered at the tables.
The colors do not tell us whether every household had enough. They tell the next keeper what was set aside and what was given away.
The public total lists fruit gathered, while the margin holds seed kept for the next planting.
If I combine them, I count the same season twice: once as food and again as the beginning of another harvest.
The graft came from a branch that has not been tested through winter. It may fruit well in this bed and fail somewhere else.
Write down the one plot we actually observed. Leave the promise of a regional yield for a trial that has not happened.
The higher line followed a storm; the lower scratch was present before it. Neither one alone shows how much water the garden used.
I am recording their dates and conditions instead of drawing one smooth line through two unequal observations.
A recording can preserve a pitch and still remove the moment when someone chose to sing. I log the room and the invitation separately.
You may use the interval in the model, but do not copy a person's voice into a chart unless they agreed to that use.
The koi carried a faint vibration in its scales today. We can note the sample and the pool without assigning it a meaning.
One catch cannot tell us whether the vibration is common, seasonal or connected to the signal we heard.

Ta ghi cả hai mặt và giữ khoảng cách với tro nóng; hiện vật không nói ai đã đặt nó xuống.
Lò nguội khi ta tới, còn dấu bò của Salamander dừng trước chân bệ. Nhiệt còn trong tro không cho biết ai đã đốt lửa trước đó.
Ta để riêng mẫu than và vệt vảy. Hai dấu được tìm cạnh nhau, nhưng có thể có thời điểm khác nhau.
Lứa thứ hai có lá dài hơn vì luống được che gió. Ta giữ lại một nhánh cùng ghi chú, để vụ sau Mira có thể thay cách che.
Hai lần thu hoạch chưa đủ chứng minh khí hậu đã đổi; chúng chỉ cho thấy chăm sóc khác nhau tạo kết quả khác.
Blackreed Trout cắn mồi ở mép nước có bóng mái cầu. Vảy ướt giữ một dải sáng xanh, còn mực nước đã thấp hơn vạch đá hôm qua.
Ta ghi nơi và giờ bắt; một con cá không cho ta biết cả đàn đã chuyển đi đâu.
Mẻ này dịu hơn hôm qua vì Rowan để nước nguội trước khi thả lá. Viết cả nhiệt độ tương đối, không chỉ tên thuốc.
Ai uống cũng có thể nói vị quá đắng hoặc quá ngọt; ta sẽ sửa công thức theo người thử, không theo một lời khen duy nhất.
Moonwort ở luống sát tường giữ được phấn trên lá, còn luống ngoài hiên đọng nước mưa. Harper cần biết vị trí trước khi thử tín hiệu.
Ta gửi cả lá đạt và lá dập; một phép thử công khai phải ghi phần nó không dùng được.
Mẻ Phấn Dấu Mưa bám rõ trên đá nhám nhưng mờ trên gỗ ướt. Harper có thể chọn vật liệu thử ở hai điểm, không lấy màu phấn làm lời hứa tín hiệu luôn nhìn thấy.
Ghi lượng Moonwort và đồng tro đã dùng để lần sau pha lại được.
Có người muốn đánh dấu mình đã tới; người khác chỉ cần chỗ ngủ mà không muốn tên lưu trong bảng. Tôi sẽ phát chăn trước rồi hỏi từng người.
Một ô trống là thông tin chưa được trao, không phải một người còn thiếu mà chúng ta có quyền đi tìm.
Ba hàng này để dành cho số chăn chưa kiểm lại, không phải ba người biến mất. Khi nhận thêm đồ, tôi ghi giờ và người giao.
Nếu ai muốn tự ghi tên, tôi sẽ để họ cầm bút. Bảng này giúp chia việc; nó không phải cổng vào nơi trú.
Mình chọn dựng chỗ trú trước. Mira đã gom người về giếng, còn Gideon cần thêm tay nâng khung mái; dấu chân phía đông có thể chờ một lượt.
Không phải mình quên vết tích. Người đang đứng ngoài sân cần mái che ngay bây giờ.
Mình theo dấu về phía đông trước khi gió phủ mất đường. Gideon có thể đưa mọi người tới mái hiên; mình sẽ quay lại với điều đã tìm thấy.
Đây là thứ tự việc làm, không phải câu trả lời ai gây ra cuộc đột kích.
